land.text: the far south of Mesopotamia lost to Ilum-ma-ili: the marsh core, Dhi-Qar and Basra, and Uruk ("Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that"); Nippur and Isin, which the Sealand takes in -1721, are not in this land

predecessors.note: The Sealand page: the dynasty "had broken free of the Old Babylonian Empire".

land.text: the Sealand, which Ulam-Buriash "conquered ... incorporated into Babylonia": the marsh core, Dhi-Qar and Basra, Uruk, and Nippur and Isin

successors.note: Kassite Babylonia; the Sealand page gives no year BC for the conquest.

capitals.name: Dur-Enlil (site unknown; Lagash, Nippur and Tell Dehaila are proposed)
capitals.note: "The home city of the Sealand Dynasty is currently unknown"; "Modern thinking is that the capital was a Dūr-Enlil" but it is unclear whether this matches. The dot is placed at Lagash (Tell al-Hiba), the page's E'urukuga speculation, and is not a located capital.

union.text: Sumer, "control of Sumer for the next 300 years"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1732..-1701: Cliopatria starts the Sealand in -1700 but the page dates the dynasty "very speculatively c. 1732-1475 BC (MC)" and Samsu-iluna's page puts Ilum-ma-ili's revolt in his years 18-29 (1732-1721), "founded the First Dynasty of Sea-Land, which would remain in control of Sumer for the next 300 years". Cliopatria's marsh shape plus Sumer.

8,320 km2 around the marsh and Gulf head (46.6-48.1 E, 29.7-30.8 N) is the core only. The page finds "Sealand pottery ... at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that", Nippur was "conquered ... late in Samsu-iluna's reign", and Samsu-iluna's page gives Ilum-ma-ili "control of Sumer" while Ur, Uruk and Larsa were "largely or completely abandoned". The corrected shape adds Sumer south of 32.3 N; the true extent may be smaller (page silent on boundaries).
13,101 km2 (-1600..-1501), same correction: Ayadaragalama made offerings to "Inanna of Larsa" and a legal tablet of Larsa is dated to Ilum-ma-ili, so Larsa lay within reach.

correction.text: the marsh core and Sumer; valid -1500..-1461

keyframe_review.note: 15,392 km2: valid to -1461. "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled" (Kassites page); the Sealand page ends the dynasty c. 1475 and the Babylonia page dates Ulamburiash's attack "around 1450 BC". Cliopatria runs the row to -1401, 59 years past 1460.

region.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa) and Uruk: "Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that"

ledger.note: c. 1732 BC: Ilum-ma-ili founds the Sealand dynasty in the far south. The page dates it "very speculatively c. 1732-1475 BC (MC)" and names Ilum-ma-ilī "the founder of the dynasty" without a founding year; Samsu-iluna's page places the revolt in his years 18-29 (1732-1721), after the pretender Rim-Sin II (year 9) failed. Land (fx-48, 3 Nov 2026): the marsh core plus Dhi-Qar, Basra and Uruk (60 km), replacing the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle (about 404,000 km2 of Arabia and Khuzestan): the page finds Sealand pottery "at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that"; the page is silent on boundaries. Nippur and Isin join in -1721 (data/patches/m1800-m1701.json events/0).

region.text: the Sealand incorporated into Babylonia: the marsh core, Dhi-Qar and Basra, Uruk, and Nippur and Isin

ledger.note: c. 1460 BC: the Kassites conquer the Sealand. "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled"; Ulam-Buriash, brother of Kashtiliash III, "conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia" (Sealand page), Ea-gamil "fled to Elam"; Agum III then attacked it again, destroying a temple in Dur-Enlil. Land (fx-48, 3 Nov 2026) is the corrected Sealand land (marsh core, Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk 60 km, Nippur 40 km, Isin 40 km), not the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N rectangle.

wars.name: Ilum-ma-ili's revolt
wars.outcome: Ilum-ma-ili "attacked and brought about the defeat of (Samsu-iluna's) army" (Sealand page) and Nippur "recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king" by Samsu-iluna's death (Samsu-iluna page); Abi-ešuḫ "set out to conquer Ilum-ma-ilī" without result.
wars.note: Abi-eshuh's and Ammi-ditana's attempts (the latter destroyed "the city wall of Der/Udinim built by the army of Damqi-ilišu") have no year BC on the page.

wars.name: Kassite conquest of the Sealand
wars.outcome: Ulam-Buriash conquered the Sealand and incorporated it into Babylonia; Agum III attacked it and destroyed a temple in Dur-Enlil. A year-name of Ayadaragalama mentions a "great ring against the Kalšu (Kassite) enemy".

certainty.note: The dynasty's extent is not on any page: the corrected shape is a reading of "Sumer", with the marshes and the Gulf head as the sure core.

sources.title: Samsu-iluna
sources.note: Ilum-ma-ili's revolt in Samsu-iluna's years 18-29, "control of Sumer for the next 300 years", Nippur, abandonment of cities. Read for babylonia.

sources.title: First Sealand dynasty
sources.note: Dynasty "very speculatively c. 1732-1475 BC (MC)"; capital unknown; finds at Girsu, Uruk, Lagash; Nippur; Ulam-Buriash and Agum III. No infobox.

sources.title: Kassites
sources.note: "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC". Read for babylonia.

notes:
IDENTITY. Cliopatria shape is -1700..-1401; the page span is c. 1732 to 1475 (middle chronology, "very speculatively"); the Kassites page gives the fall in 1460, so the dossier is -1732..-1460 to match babylonia's loss and gain. Cliopatria's extra 59 years (-1459..-1401) go to Babylonia. Capital unknown.
EXTENT. The three Cliopatria shapes (8-15 k km2) cover the marsh and the Gulf head only. Samsu-iluna's page says the Sealand held Sumer for 300 years and Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili; the Sealand page itself has pottery at Girsu, Uruk and Lagash and nowhere north, and Samsu-iluna says Ur, Uruk and Larsa were "largely or completely abandoned". Corrections add Sumer south of 32.3 N at confidence 2; a gap-filler with archaeology could shrink it. Kuwait/Iran parts of the Cliopatria shape are unverified.
PAGES. 1 own page (First Sealand dynasty) plus Samsu-iluna and Kassites, read for babylonia (budget 1-2). No infobox, so no area comparison.
NOT REACHED. No dated war of Abi-eshuh or Ammi-ditana (no year BC on the page). Dynasty V of Babylon, "dynasty of the Sealand" (1025-1004 BC, Babylonia page), is a later Babylonian dynasty with the same label, not this state.
